chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, from Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Sa'id, from Amr ibn Sahl, from Harun ibn Kharijah, from Jabir al-Ja'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever seeks forgiveness from God seventy times after the dawn prayer, God will forgive him, even if he committed seventy thousand sins that day. And whoever committed more than seventy thousand sins, there is no good in him. And in another narration, 'seven hundred sins'.
ai.seo_question: How many times should one seek forgiveness after dawn prayer to be forgiven for sins?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the transformative power of consistent post-Fajr devotion, noting that the specific number of seventy serves as a symbolic threshold for divine mercy rather than a rigid cap. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on the dawn prayer as a critical juncture for spiritual renewal, where persistent repentance can cleanse even a significant accumulation of daily transgressions.
